items.excerpt: Major AI companies have signed a voluntary code of practice and begun watermarking their outputs, and the EU AI Act now pushes detectability by default. MIDiA argues watermarks could reset how listeners and platforms treat AI-made tracks, making 'human-made' a signal creators can actually carry.
items.title: Do watermarks spell the end of AI content proliferation?

items.excerpt: Apple is preparing a 'Made With AI' tag for Apple Music that would apply whenever 'a material portion of the content' was generated with AI. The disclosure would run through distributor-facing transparency tags, putting the burden of declaration on the people uploading the music.
items.title: Apple Music will reportedly label any AI-made tracks later this year

items.excerpt: Apple Music will start showing 'Made With AI' labels on tracks later in 2026, built on the AI transparency tags it gave labels and distributors earlier this year. CMU walks through what counts as 'material' AI use and who has to declare it.
items.title: Apple Music to start labelling tracks 'Made With AI'

items.excerpt: Apple Music is rolling out a mandatory 'Made With AI' label, and gearnews pairs it with the uncomfortable number behind it: over a third of uploads are already fully AI-generated but barely streamed. The producer-facing question is what counts as AI use once the tag is compulsory.
items.title: Apple Music to label AI-generated songs

items.excerpt: After a decade of point tools, the argument is that independent artists need an AI-connected operating system that links catalogue, data and release actions instead of another dashboard. The op-ed sketches what an agentic layer under an artist's workflow would actually have to do.
items.title: Independent Artists Need an Operating System, Not Another 'Tool'

items.excerpt: Billboard says it will identify AI-generated music in its charts and editorial, leaning on creator disclosure plus new detection tooling. It is the chart side of the same transparency push now running through Apple Music, Spotify and ARIA.
items.title: Billboard Affirms Commitment to Transparency Around AI-Generated Music

items.excerpt: Luminate is adding AI-detection to its Connect platform to flag AI-generated songs and artists worldwide, and Billboard says it will use those flags in how it categorises chart entries. Detection, not self-disclosure, becomes the mechanism artists get measured by.
items.title: Billboard and Luminate promise more transparency around AI music

items.excerpt: Discovery is shifting from keyword search and metadata to listeners describing a mood or context and letting a model choose the music. For artists that changes what has to be legible about them — identity and context, not tags.
items.title: Your Next Fan May Never Search for You

items.excerpt: A loose network of musicians has turned into amateur detectives, hunting down 'AI grifters' passing generated tracks off as human work. The profile shows the listening heuristics and forensic habits they've built to spot AI slop.
items.title: Meet the Musicians Leading the Anti-AI 'Callout Culture'

items.excerpt: The Denon DJ Prime 4 G2 adds a big processing jump and real-time stem separation on the standalone unit, letting DJs pull acapellas and instrumentals live without pre-rendering. Neural source separation moves from laptop software into the controller itself.
items.title: Denon DJ Prime 4 G2: multi-function pads and real-time stems
